current_catalog_reference.meaning: existing taxonomy identity; not an executable composer route

scope: Source-grounded research profile for a family of South African electronic dance-music practices. Not a single prescriptive formula, genre classifier, or claim of cultural authenticity.

historical_context.summary: Published scholarship situates Amapiano in South African township dance-music histories and discusses relationships with earlier forms including marabi, mbaqanga, bubblegum and kwaito. Accounts differ on origin dates, places, naming and influence; preserve multiple attributed histories rather than a single origin story.

claims.statement: Amapiano emerged in South African township contexts around the early 2010s; one scholarly account places its emergence around 2012.
claims.limit: Do not turn an approximate scholarly framing into a definitive origin date or single-place origin.

claims.statement: Its histories are connected to older South African township music, including marabi, mbaqanga, bubblegum and kwaito, alongside international musical influences and new production technologies.
claims.limit: Influence is not a linear family tree and does not make these traditions interchangeable.

candidate_identity_axes.observation: Scholarly descriptions identify extended instrumental openings and gradual addition of musical layers in some Amapiano releases.
candidate_identity_axes.operational_hypothesis: A style-conditioned composer should be able to plan and vary a long-form layer-entry/subtraction trajectory rather than defaulting to immediate verse-chorus entry.
candidate_identity_axes.disconfirming_case: Practitioner-identified Amapiano examples whose arrangement does not use extended instrumental introductions.

candidate_identity_axes.observation: Accounts describe prominent keyboard/piano material, pads and bass sounds, including the distinctive log-drum bass timbre in many representative productions.
candidate_identity_axes.operational_hypothesis: Represent keyboard roles, low-frequency melodic/percussive bass roles and layered pads independently; test role interaction rather than requiring a fixed instrument list.
candidate_identity_axes.disconfirming_case: Practitioner-identified examples with reduced piano/log-drum presence or alternative instrumentation.

candidate_identity_axes.observation: Amapiano is described as dance-oriented and electronically produced, with local and global groove influences.
candidate_identity_axes.operational_hypothesis: Represent the relationship between pulse, bass/log-drum phrases, percussion, syncopation and phrase-level density as separate, testable layers.
candidate_identity_axes.disconfirming_case: A single quantized pattern or one fixed BPM/meter fails to explain practitioner-selected examples.

candidate_identity_axes.observation: Published accounts describe piano and jazz-influenced harmonic colour among Amapiano's resources.
candidate_identity_axes.operational_hypothesis: Support keyboard voicings and harmonic motion as optional identity-bearing dimensions without imposing one chord loop or treating jazz influence as a sufficient genre definition.
candidate_identity_axes.disconfirming_case: Amapiano examples where harmony is sparse, static or not keyboard-led.

candidate_identity_axes.observation: Scholarship discusses Amapiano as a technologically mediated, collaborative dance-music practice involving production, performance and dissemination contexts.
candidate_identity_axes.operational_hypothesis: Keep producer/DJ, instrumental, vocal and performance roles representable without assuming every recording uses the same division of labour.
candidate_identity_axes.disconfirming_case: Practitioner accounts that reject the proposed role decomposition for a given scene or substyle.

nearest_neighbour_questions.question: Which keyboard, bass, groove, arrangement and scene-context relationships are considered identity-bearing by practitioners, rather than merely shared electronic-dance conventions?
Which rhythmic, arrangement and production continuities are historically related, and which traits distinguish Amapiano in particular?
How do melody/harmony prominence, low-frequency roles, rhythmic organization and arrangement trajectory differ across practitioner-selected examples?
Which local production and rhythmic exchanges are influence, hybridization, shared practice or explicit distinction? Preserve multiple attributed accounts.

non_inferences: Do not require every Amapiano composition to contain a log drum, piano lead, vocalist, fixed intro length, fixed BPM, fixed chord progression or identical drum grid.
Do not treat Amapiano as a single homogeneous style or erase scene, era, producer and substyle variation.
Do not infer artist, ethnicity, language, community membership or provenance from audio features.
Do not infer historical influence or cultural authenticity from musical feature similarity.
Do not use commercial recordings for training, public fixture redistribution or commercial evaluation without rights appropriate to each purpose.
required_next_evidence: Practitioner-reviewed vocabulary and identity-bearing dimensions across more than one Amapiano scene/substyle.
Rights-cleared examples with composition, recording, performer, producer and usage scope kept distinct.
Contrastive examples against Kwaito, deep/soulful house, Gqom and locally nominated neighbours.
A symbolic profile contract that marks observed, inferred, inherited and unresolved fields separately.
A controlled style-identity study under performer, instrumentation and renderer variation.

limitations: historical framing is multivocal; does not prove a single origin date or universal musical recipe

supports: extended instrumental openings and gradual layer addition in discussed examples
limitations: examples and scope are bounded; features are not requirements for every track

limitations: review full text and practitioner accounts before deriving narrow production or composition rules
